title: Just Walk By My Side
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Grades A Man's Accent, A Palace's Hospitality, And Everyone's Alibi, And Lights One Small Candle
standfirst: Jimmy Dobson walked into a gold country with a button in his pocket, explained the plan to a king, did an accent at a palace, lied badly to a plumber made of memory and climbed into a cannon, and asked to be taken back out. I have a lot of feelings, most of them at his expense. The grown-up version of this is on the analysis page. This is the loud one.
pullQuote: A man who tells you he is lost while holding a detonator is not lost. He is early.
filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — filed late; the day it describes is 20 Harvestide (estimated hour)

sections.heading: 'I've Been Lost Here For Ages,' Said The Man With The Detonator
sections.body:
Let me set the scene. A stranger in a red cap opens his arms on a gold road and says **"Youve-a wondered far from home"** and Jimmy Dobson answers **"oh thank god I've been lost here for ages."**

Thank GOD. Ages. Look at him. Look at the little crinkle of relief. I almost bought it, and I have SOLD that exact line to a border guard.

He was not lost. He had a button in his pocket and a Koopa assault on a timer. **That is not lost. That is a delivery.** Lost people don't know what time anything is going to blow up.

And the HOST. I need to talk about the host. His whole opening is a rhyme, and the rhyme is **"through my veneer your never a-lone."** *Your* never alone. YOUR. It is *you're*. The most dangerous thing in the Mushroom Kingdom is a man with a thousand-year smile and a grammar problem, and nobody in this file has corrected him, so I am doing it now, in the permanent record: **you're**. Two words. One apostrophe. It is a contraction.

*WAH! He also said 'no benevolence' in the first minute, which is the most honest sentence in the document. Jimmy heard it the way you hear the safety announcement on a plane.*

sections.heading: Okay, Letsa Go
sections.body:
At the crucial moment, Jimmy takes the button out, looks at it, looks at the palace, and says, in the host's own accent: **"okay letsa go."**

Reader, I sat with that for a full minute.

A man walking into a gold palace to detonate a monarchy decides to do it **in an impression**. He had two hours of free character development on that road and he used it to learn the voice. It is the bravest and stupidest thing in the file until the cannon, and the cannon is a long way off, so give it some respect.

Here is what I think happened. Jimmy was frightened, so Jimmy got rude. Jimmy was very frightened, so Jimmy got funny. Jimmy was more frightened than THAT, so Jimmy did an *accent*. It is the third stage of grief. It comes after bargaining and before pizza.

I have done the impression of an enemy to myself in a mirror. I did it for TENNIS. I was not walking into a palace. Jimmy: respect, and also **no**.

sections.heading: Reviewing The Hospitality: One Star, Would Not Be Eaten Again
sections.body:
I have stayed in worse places. I have stayed in nothing places. But I have never read a hospitality sheet where the host *promises* four things and delivers *one*, and the one is the King.

**Dining halls** — promised. Not seen.
**Gardens** — promised. Not seen.
**The good room for sleeping** — promised, with a wink. Not seen. I would like the wink back.
**The King** — delivered, immediately, at the top of a staircase that starts ringing doorbells BY ITSELF.

Notes from the guest book:

- *The gate lowers itself and groans like gold grinding on gold.* Fine. Dramatic. Two stars for the entrance.
- *The courtyard doors close behind you with a finality that echoes.* Minus one star, I wasn't consulted.
- *The torches have no visible fuel.* Minus the other one. Whoever's paying that gas bill is not a person.
- *The host walks faster the higher you climb.* That is not a tour. That is a cart being pushed up a ramp.

**Final rating: one star for the shine. Do not stay. Do not eat the creatures. They snap their beaks at you when you refuse to play, and Jimmy refused, and he was RIGHT.**

sections.heading: He Explained The Plan To The King's Face
sections.body:
Okay. THE BUTTON.

The King asks, in a voice you feel in your sternum, **"MARIO... IS THIS THE TRAVELER YOU PROMISED?"** And Jimmy, who has been squeezing a pocket for two hours like it owes him money, presses it. In the room. In the throne room. In the **ROOM**.

And then he *explains*. Out loud. To the host who is trying to stop him. **"Oh I know and its planned, the koopa troops are coming."**

That is not a plan. That is a monologue. In every heist film in the archive, the guy with the button presses it in a *different building* and then walks away looking at his watch. Jimmy pressed it standing in front of the target, and then read out the next three steps like a flight attendant.

*WAH! I would like to say I would have done it better. I would have pressed it from the roof. With a hat on. With the receipt.*

And then, I swear to you, the roof opens on cue. Bowser drops in on a Koopa car. Paratroopas fall. Hammer Bros line the rafters. The King calls it treason and a stain, in that order. The host screams **"That's not-a how this works!"**

Mario, buddy. This is EXACTLY how it works. You are the one who put a king on a throne in a building with a roof that opens.

sections.heading: Everyone Brought A Different Party
sections.body:
My favourite detail in the whole raid is that the invasion has no theme.

Bowser: **"GO FOR THE KING!"**
The troopers: **"RAID THE TREASURY!"**
The squad leaders: **"We're on official business!"** (There is a bomb.)
The King: **"BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT!"**
Jimmy: **"its planned."**

Five people, five reasons, and ONE roof. It is a wedding where everyone thinks they are the bride. The hammer bros threw hammers. Somebody, probably Bowser, got hit by his own side's hammers and swore at them. The troopers wanted GOLD. That is the one honest line: *RAID THE TREASURY.* Pure. Uncomplicated. The only soldier in that building who knew exactly why he got out of bed.

I am a professional and I would like to say that this is not how you run a raid. A raid is a schedule with a grudge. This was a **group chat**.

*WAH! Bowser said later that he 'missed a few pieces from the briefing.' A king of the Koopas who did not READ HIS BRIEFING. I have never been so comforted and so alarmed in the same breath.*

sections.heading: 'Uhh No.'
sections.body:
The host turns to Jimmy in the middle of a collapsing palace and asks, with a bomb going off at his back door, **"DID YOU-A DO THIS?"**

And Jimmy says: **"uhh no."**

I need everyone to appreciate how much work *uhh* is doing. It is a single syllable of pure panic, and it is aimed at a man he PRESSED A BUTTON NEXT TO four minutes ago and then SAID OUT LOUD that he did it.

I have forged forty documents. I have lied to a notary while the notary was on fire. I know what a good lie looks like, and it looks like **boredom**. A good lie is delivered like a bus timetable. Jimmy delivered his like a man who has just been asked, in front of his mother, whether he took the last biscuit, and has crumbs on his shirt.

And it WORKED. The host stares for one suspicious heartbeat and then a tremor shakes the floor and bails him out. Jimmy owes the earthquake dinner.

sections.heading: Why Are You Black And White (Asked In A Tunnel, During A Bombing)
sections.body:
Two hours. Two HOURS of walking next to a man in grey, through a country made of gold, and *then* Jimmy goes: **"Mario, I've never asked this, but why are you black and white?"**

In a tunnel. During a collapse. After a bomb. Right when the man is trying to save him.

I love him. I'm sorry. I love him. It is the least tactical question ever asked, and the question every single one of us was already screaming at the page. I screamed it at the *courtyard*. Jimmy waited for the **fire**.

And the host, bless him, answers properly. **"It's-a because this place isn't real."** Then: **"The colors only happen for those who belong in-a the frame."** Then, when Jimmy asks if he's really Mario, the line that made me put the pen down: **"Mario is... well, Mario is a memory."**

Same. I am a memory. I am a memory of a tennis victory nobody gave me. Somewhere in the Mushroom Kingdom there is a podium with my name carved into its absence, and I think about it every day.

*WAH! Evil Mario is an actor. Director Mario is a boss. This Mario is a memory in a cap. The file has three Marios and not one of them is employed by a person who brought a lunch.*

sections.heading: 'I Am On Your Side, Dumbass'
sections.body:
I have to give Jimmy credit, and it is going to cost me, so let me do it quickly.

In the middle of a collapse, he hears a Koopa Troopa crying under a ceiling, and he goes *back*. Nobody asked him. The trooper doesn't know him. The trooper is part of the army he came to help burn a building down. And Jimmy grabs him by the shell, and hauls, and when the trooper screams **"Get your hands off me, civilian!"** he pulls out the badge and says the single most affectionate insult in the archive:

**"I am on your side dumbass."**

That's it. That's the entire speech. A rescue that sounds like a mugging. The trooper, I note, is also not grateful. He says **"watch the shell! Damn it, watch the shell!"** while being saved from DEATH. They deserve each other. If they ever meet again I would like to be in the room with a camera and a plate of crisps.

*WAH! The badge worked. It worked on a soldier who had never been told there was an extraction. So either the badge is real and nobody read the memo, or the memo is real and nobody printed the badge. Both of those are Bowser.*

sections.heading: He Climbed Into The Cannon, And Then He Wanted Out
sections.body:
We have reached the cannon.

Jimmy takes the cannonball. It is made of ink. The cannon is made of ink. The sky is ink. The monster is *definitely* ink. And Jimmy decides the correct response to an ink monster is to **climb into an ink cannon with an ink ball and be fired at it.**

Let me give you Jimmy's whole sequence of sentences, in order, as filed:

1. *"I'll put an end to this."*
2. *"I climb into the cannon with the cannonball."*
3. *"oof, this was a bad idea."*
4. *"okay this is a bad idea put me back out put me back out aaaa"*

There. That is a man's whole character arc in under ten seconds. Confidence, commitment, regret, begging. It is the plot of every New Year's resolution I have ever made.

The monster, who has been waiting two hours for someone dramatic, says **"THE PROTAGONIST ALWAYS LOSES IN THE END!"** Excellent line. Villain's pick. Seven out of ten, docked three for 'granite teeth' being a reach. And then Jimmy sinks into a throat made of charcoal and the thing says **"OOOH... THAT TICKLES!"**

*WAH! I have been swallowed once, by a Chain Chomp, in a sponsored segment. I did not get a line. I got an invoice.*

sections.heading: And The Sentence The Roof Ate
sections.body:
One tiny serious thing, and then I'll go back to being unbearable.

In the throne room, the King shouting treason, Jimmy tries to say: **"after Peach's deat—"**

And the roof opens before he gets to the *h*.

I want that sentence. I want it more than I want the podium. I would trade a tennis trophy for the *rest of that clause.* Jimmy knew something about what came after Peach, he was going to say it to a king and a Koopa in the same breath, and a roof said **no**.

If you are keeping score: the most important thing anyone said all afternoon was interrupted by **architecture**.

sections.heading: Waluigi's Scorecard For Jimmy Dobson
sections.body:
Out of ten, in no particular order, with the reasoning left in the margins where it belongs:

**Courage — 9.** Climbed into a cannon. Docked one because he asked to come out.
**Planning — 2.** Told the plan to the King. Also did not know the plan.
**Accent — 4.** An impression, held for one sentence, with a stable lisp on 'letsa'.
**Lying — 1.** *Uhh no.* Next.
**Compassion — 8.** He went back for the trooper. He called him a dumbass. It still counts.
**Curiosity — 10.** He asked why the plumber was black and white. It took two hours. It was perfect.
**Survival — unknown.** He is in the mouth.

**Overall: 6.** Would not hire. Would send a card.

And a candle. A small one. I do not give candles lightly; I have a *Rule*. But there is a man in a mouth made of charcoal, holding a cannonball made of ink, who said *put me back out*, and in all my years of filing the stupidest people in the Mushroom Kingdom, that is the first time one of them has said *I would like to go back.* That is a human being. That is the only part of the whole account that I believed.

*WAH! If anyone finds him, please do not tell me. I would rather keep the candle.*
